query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with a trace amount (around 0.2 at.%) of boron will enhance its load-bearing integrity while preserving its intrinsic caloric performance under applied field or pressure-field operation.
generation.material_initial_state: The base (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response under external stimuli but suffers from poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Introduce a minor boron addition during alloy synthesis, ensuring homogeneous distribution (e.g., during melting and homogenization).
generation.conditions: Tests to be performed under the same applied magnetic field and pressure-field regimes (over temperatures that span the alloy’s caloric phase transformation) and under similar mechanical loading as the operational refrigeration conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron is expected to segregate to grain boundaries, leading to strengthened intergranular cohesion and refined microstructure.
generation.mechanism: The segregation of boron to grain boundaries lowers their energy and acts to inhibit crack initiation and propagation, thus increasing mechanical integrity. At the low concentration used, boron should not disrupt the phase transitions responsible for the caloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: The boron-alloyed material will show a statistically significant improvement in fracture toughness and reduced crack propagation while retaining caloric performance (i.e., similar isothermal entropy change and phase transformation characteristics) compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.baseline: The undoped (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, known to possess good caloric response but limited load-bearing integrity.
generation.boundary: The intervention is applicable as long as the operating magnetic field, pressure, temperature, and mechanical loading conditions remain within the bounds defined for refrigeration use. Deviations (e.g., extreme fields or temperatures beyond the alloy’s transformation range) are not considered.
generation.uncertainty: It is uncertain whether boron at the proposed concentration might interact with the complex high-entropy matrix in unforeseen ways, potentially affecting the crystallographic order or the caloric phase transformation if local segregations become too pronounced.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one batch of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy doped with ~0.2 at.% boron and a control batch without boron, processed under identical conditions. Subject both sets to identical applied-field and pressure-field operational tests as well as mechanical integrity tests.
measurements: Fracture toughness (e.g., via standardized bending or indentation tests)
Caloric response (e.g., isothermal entropy change or temperature change under field/pressure)
Phase transformation characteristics (using DSC or XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped alloy does not show a minimum of a 10% increase in fracture toughness or exhibits more than a 5% reduction in caloric performance relative to the undoped baseline, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
